title: Why Did It Happen?
objectives: I can use because to tell why something happened.
I can use so to tell what happened as a result.
I can use if to talk about what could happen.
I can name the reason or the cause when I explain.
rationale: Because, so, and if are the smallest words that carry reasoning, and first graders need them to explain almost anything. Reason, cause, and happen name the idea those small words express, so the unit teaches the thinking and the language together. It builds on the order words from unit 2 (then, finally) and on explain from unit 1, since a good explanation gives both the order and the reason.

words.ex: I wore a coat because it was cold.
words.ex2: The baby cried because she was hungry.
words.nonExample: "We ran, then we sat" tells what came next, not why.

apps.academic: Use because to give a reason.
apps.spoken: I like it because it is soft.
apps.writing: Write because and then tell why.

cloze.s: The ground is wet ___ it rained all night.

cloze2.s: Ana is smiling ___ she got a gold star on her paper.

misuse.s: The ice melted because it was very cold.
misuse.why: Ice melts when it is warm. Cold is not a real reason for melting.

visual.alt: An arrow from a reason to the thing that it explains.

words.def: A word that tells the result.
words.ex: It was raining, so we took umbrellas.
words.ex2: The box was heavy, so Dad helped carry it.

apps.academic: Use so to tell what happened next.
apps.spoken: I was tired, so I went to bed.
apps.writing: Write a short sentence with so to show a result.

cloze.s: The cat was hungry, ___ it ate all of its food.

cloze2.s: It started to snow, ___ we put on our hats and gloves.

misuse.s: I was very thirsty, so I did not drink any water.
misuse.why: A thirsty person drinks. This result does not fit the cause.

visual.alt: An arrow from something that happened to its result.

words.def: A word that tells what could be true.
words.ex: If it rains, we will stay inside.
words.ex2: You can have a snack if you finish your work.

apps.academic: If you finish, read a book.
apps.writing: Use if to tell what could happen.

cloze.s: ___ it snows tomorrow, we can build a snowman.

cloze2.s: You will get wet ___ you play in the rain without a coat.

misuse.s: I ate my lunch, so I said, "If I ate it, I will eat it now."
misuse.why: If is for something that is not sure yet. You already know you ate it.

visual.alt: The word if is a small function word, so it has no picture.

words.def: What tells why something happens or is done.
words.ex: My reason for being late was the bus.
words.ex2: Give one reason you like the park.
words.nonExample: "I like it" says that you like it, but does not give a reason.

apps.academic: Give a reason for your answer.
apps.writing: Write one reason that makes your idea strong.

cloze.s: Dad told me the ___ for the closed road: a tree had fallen.

cloze2.s: What is your ___ for wearing a hat? Is the sun out?

misuse.s: My reason for wearing a coat was that it was hot outside.
misuse.why: A coat keeps you warm. Hot weather is not a reason to wear one.

visual.alt: A child thinking with a light bulb above their head.

words.def: To take place at a certain time.
words.ex: What will happen if we plant this seed?
words.ex2: A funny thing happened at lunch today.
words.nonExample: A chair sitting still does not happen; it just sits.

apps.academic: What will happen next in the story?
apps.writing: Tell what happened in the story.

cloze.s: Look at the dark clouds. I think rain will ___ soon.

cloze2.s: A funny thing ___ at the zoo: the parrot said hello!

misuse.s: My name is happening on my shirt.
misuse.why: Happen is for events that take place. A name on a shirt does not take place.

visual.alt: Dark rain clouds with a question mark beside them.

words.def: The thing that makes something happen.
words.ex: The cause of the puddle was the rain.
words.ex2: A loose shoelace was the cause of Sam's trip.
words.nonExample: A puddle is not the cause of rain; it is what the rain made.

apps.academic: Find the cause of the problem.
apps.writing: Write the cause and then the effect.

cloze.s: Slipping on ice was the ___ of Pablo's fall.

cloze2.s: A broken wheel was the ___ of why the wagon stopped.

misuse.s: Sitting in a warm room was the cause of the snow outside.
misuse.why: A cause makes something happen. A warm room cannot make snow fall outside.

visual.alt: Rain falling and making a puddle.

passage.title: The Muddy Paws
paras: Max the dog came inside with muddy paws. Rosa asked Dad for the reason. "It rained, so the yard is wet," said Dad, "and the rain was the cause of the mud." "What will happen if we do not wipe his paws?" asked Rosa. "We will find mud on the rug," said Dad. They got a towel because nobody wanted a muddy rug.

qs.q: What was the cause of the mud?
qs.why: Dad says the rain was the cause of the mud.

qs.q: Why did they get a towel?
choices: They did not want mud on the rug.
qs.why: The story says nobody wanted a muddy rug.

qs.q: Rosa asked Dad for the reason. What did she want to know?
choices: Why Max had mud on his paws
qs.why: A reason tells why, and Rosa wanted to know why Max's paws were muddy.

write.prompt: Draw a time when something happened to you. Tell why it happened. Use because.

study.task: Pick a card with because, so, or if. Say a sentence that uses the word. Tell a partner what the word does.

sentences: Say a sentence that tells why you were happy. Start with I was happy because.
Say a sentence with so. Tell what happened after.
Say a sentence with if about a rainy day.

combine.model: The cup fell, so it broke.
Mia was sad because her kite broke.

discuss: What is a good reason to wear a coat?
What could happen if you forget your lunch?
produce.explain: Explain why we wash our hands before lunch. Use because.

constructed.prompt: Tell one thing you did today and give a reason. Use because and the word reason.
look: gives a reason that makes sense
constructed.model: I wore my boots because it was muddy outside. My reason was to keep my feet dry.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a time something happened. Say what the cause was.
constructed.model: A puddle happened on the floor. The cause was a spilled cup of water.

teacher.overview: Children learn three small words that join ideas (because, so, if) and three words that name the thinking behind them (reason, happen, cause). The unit revisits then, finally, and explain.

notes.va.because.conj: Give the effect and ask for the reason: 'The grass is wet.' 'Because ___.' Children often say because without a reason, so ask 'What makes it true?'
notes.va.so.conj: So points forward to the result. Pair it with because: 'It rained, so the grass is wet' and 'The grass is wet because it rained' say the same fact in two orders.
notes.va.if.conj: If is about what is not sure yet. Use real classroom 'what if' questions. Avoid using if for things already known.
notes.va.reason.n: A reason answers why. Hold up two sentences, one with a reason and one without, and ask which one tells why.
notes.va.happen.v: Happen is for events, not objects. Act out events and say what happened. Pair with the picture of a storm to link to the weather unit.
notes.va.cause.n: Introduce cause with pairs of pictures: cause on the left, what happened on the right. Say 'The rain caused the puddle.' The noun is the target; the verb is a bonus.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The floor is wet. What happened? A cup fell, and the water spilled. The cause was the cup. The reason I need a towel is that the floor is wet. If I do not wipe it, someone might slip, so I will wipe it right now because I want everyone to be safe.'
discuss: What happened when you forgot something important?
What is one cause of a rainbow?
misconceptions: Because and so mean the same thing in the same place in a sentence.
A reason has to be a long sentence.
If means that something already happened.
Cause and reason are two different things.
extend: Children draw a cause-and-effect pair on a folded paper and share it with a partner.
Play 'What if?': ask a what-if question and children answer with if and so.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit because and so the next day by giving pairs of sentences, again at one week, and use them whenever children explain. Reason and cause return in the weather unit.

wida.oral: Partner A says what happened (The grass is wet). Partner B gives a reason with because and a result with so.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (porque, así que, si, razón, pasar, causa) are not reviewed by a native speaker; pasar for happen may be better as suceder in some regions.
So is taught only in the result sense (a conjunction), and if only in the conditional sense, to keep each word one clear meaning.
Cause includes a verb sense in senses; the unit teaches the noun.
